subject: Workplace Skills
title: Knowing When to Escalate Beyond Your Boss
description: One-minute skill: Knowing When to Escalate Beyond Your Boss.

hook.text: An employee discovered safety violations. His boss told him to stay quiet. He escalated to HR and saved the company.

buildup.text: Bypassing your boss is a serious move. It should be rare, deliberate, and reserved for genuine ethical or safety issues.

discovery.text: Document everything before escalating. Dates, conversations, instructions, and your attempts to resolve it directly.

twist.text: Escalating minor disagreements makes you look disloyal. Escalating genuine concerns makes you look principled.

climax.text: Try to resolve directly at least twice. Document the attempts. If the issue is serious, go to HR or skip-level.

punchline.text: Try direct first. Document always. Escalate if needed.

quiz.question: When is it appropriate to escalate beyond your boss?
options: Whenever you disagree with a decision
After documenting direct attempts to resolve genuine ethical or safety issues
When you want a different assignment
